records.subject: Anatomy
records.stem: ww Which of the following is NOT a typical cause of a bitemporal hemianopia:
options: Optic glioma (Vv) Posterior cerebral artery stroke 78%
Aneurysm of the anterior communicating artery
records.explanation: A bitemporal hemianopia is most likely due to compression at the optic chiasm. This may be caused by pituitary tumour, craniopharyngioma, meningioma, optic glioma or aneurysm of the internal carotid artery. A posterior cerebral stroke will most likely result in a contralateral homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing. ; : Vv Visual Pathway ANATOMY / CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM / CRANIAL NERVE LESIONS

records.stem: Which of the following spinal tracts is involved with the control of trunk muscles: Anterior spinothalamic tract 4% (x) ateral spinothalamic tract 5% Posterior column 55% Posterior corticospinal tract 8%
records.explanation: The anterior corticospinal tract is involved with the control of axial muscles. Vv Spinal Cord Tracts ANATOMY / CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM The spinal cord has numerous groups of nerve fibers going towards and coming from the brain. These ascending and descending tracts of the spinal cord are responsible for carrying motor and sensory stimuli to and from the periphery.

records.subject: Anatomy
records.stem: ww Occlusion of which of the following blood vessels is most likely to result in a receptive dysphasia:
records.explanation: The middle cerebral artery supplies the lateral convexity of the cerebral hemisphere including a large proportion of the frontal lobe, temporal lobe and parietal lobe. Receptive dysphasia is caused by damage to the Wernicke's speech area in the dominant superior temporal lobe which is supplied by the middle cerebral artery. : v Arterial Supply of Brain
